goal.text: Cold-chain products kept within their temperature range

query.organization_type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant

kpis.text: Cold-chain shipments with a continuous temperature log (100%)
Goods with an excursion released without a quality decision (0)

beliefs: Vaccines and insulin need 2 to 8 degrees Celsius
constraints: Only the Quality Assurance Officer may release goods after an excursion

ranked_patterns.relevance: Highest relevance (0.6971): it is the same IT goal pattern - detecting and handling temperature excursions in temperature-controlled logistics. Its tasks (stream logger readings, alert on excursion, quarantine pending release), resources (data loggers, monitoring dashboard), belief (loggers record every five minutes), constraint (goods with an unresolved excursion cannot be released) and KPIs (continuous log 100%, alert acknowledged within 30 minutes) map almost one-to-one onto G04, G04-K1 and G04-K2. Its conflict resolution (automatic release for minor excursions) must be rejected in this query because the query constraint allows release only by the Quality Assurance Officer, which also drives G04-K3 (zero releases without a quality decision).

Second (0.4181): same regulated pharmaceutical domain (medicine handling, quarantine, batch records). It supplies the adaptation for G04-K3: the quarantine-release control reserved for a pharmacist role is transposed to the Quality Assurance Officer, and the 'record batch and expiry at receipt' task is transposed into recording batch plus temperature history at receipt so excursion traceability and recall are possible.

Third (0.3658): same organization type (medium-sized distributor with order management and customer-facing order confirmation). It contributes the order-to-cash interface: the confirmation/change-control discipline ('a confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request') is adapted into immutability of temperature logs and into blocking dispatch confirmation - including by the order portal and the LLM ordering assistant - for quarantined cold-chain goods, which protects G04-K3.

Fourth (0.3481): weakest match (inventory accuracy, not temperature), but its 'post every movement on scan + run cyclic counts' verification loop and its approval constraint are adapted into periodic logger calibration/coverage checks that keep G04-K1 (continuous log on 100% of cold-chain shipments) measurable and verified rather than assumed.

elements.text: Stream readings from the shipment temperature logger continuously to the cold-chain monitoring service for every cold-chain shipment, from pick-pack to hospital delivery acceptance
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the pattern task 'Stream logger readings to the monitoring service'; extended to the full order-to-delivery span so that the 100% continuous-log KPI can be evidenced for every shipment.

elements.text: Record batch number, product cold-chain class (2 to 8 degrees Celsius) and the linked temperature log identifier at receipt and at dispatch of each cold-chain line
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Record batch and expiry at receipt'; capturing batch plus log reference at receipt is what makes a shipment-level continuous log traceable and recall-ready, respecting the belief that vaccines and insulin need 2 to 8 degrees Celsius.

elements.text: Verify logger coverage and calibration before dispatch and run periodic checks of shipments with missing or interrupted readings
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Post every goods movement on scan; Run cyclic stock counts' - a verification loop that detects gaps so the 100% continuous-log target is measured, not assumed.

elements.text: Raise an excursion alert to the on-duty Responsible Pharmacist and the Quality Assurance Officer as soon as a reading leaves the 2 to 8 degrees Celsius range
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Alert the duty supervisor on an excursion'; the duty supervisor role is replaced by the pharmaceutical roles in scope and the threshold is bound to the stated belief.

elements.text: Require a timestamped acknowledgement of each excursion alert and escalate automatically if it is not acknowledged within 30 minutes
elements.justification: Operationalizes the pattern KPI 'Excursion alerts acknowledged within 30 minutes' as an explicit acknowledge-and-escalate task so G04-K2 is enforced, not only measured.

elements.text: Place affected goods automatically in quarantine status on excursion detection, pending a release decision
elements.justification: Direct reuse of 'Quarantine affected goods pending a release decision'; automatic quarantine is the precondition for zero releases without a quality decision.

elements.text: Capture the Quality Assurance Officer's release or reject decision with reason, reviewed temperature profile and electronic signature in the shipment and batch record
elements.justification: Combines the pattern's pharmacist-only quarantine release with its batch-record discipline, producing the auditable evidence needed to prove G04-K3 equals zero.

elements.text: Block the order portal and the LLM-based ordering assistant from confirming dispatch, substitution or delivery status for cold-chain lines that are in quarantine, and route such requests to the Sales Administrator
elements.justification: Adapted from the pattern's confirmation and change-control discipline ('a confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request'); prevents the customer-facing channels of this organization type from bypassing the quality decision.

elements.text: Temperature data loggers qualified for the 2 to 8 degrees Celsius range, fitted to every cold-chain shipment
elements.justification: Reuse of the pattern resource 'Temperature data loggers', qualified against the query belief on vaccines and insulin.

elements.text: Cold-chain monitoring dashboard with excursion alerting and acknowledgement tracking
elements.justification: Reuse of 'Monitoring dashboard'; it is the instrument that times and evidences the 30-minute acknowledgement KPI.

elements.text: Quarantine and batch register in the distribution system, holding temperature history and release decisions per batch
elements.justification: Adapted from the 'Pharmacy stock module' that supports quarantine and batch records; here it is the system of record for excursion-related release decisions.

elements.text: Order management module and order portal integration that exposes cold-chain hold status on order and delivery lines
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Order management module'; links the cold-chain control to the order-to-delivery flow of the parent goal.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer - sole decision maker for release or rejection of goods affected by an excursion
elements.justification: Adapted from the pattern's Quality Manager release control; the query constraint names the Quality Assurance Officer as the only authorized releaser.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist - first responder who assesses the excursion against product requirements and acknowledges the alert
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Pharmacist in Charge' and from the pattern's Duty Supervisor role, fitted to the pharmaceutical distributor in scope.

elements.text: Sales Administrator - handles customer communication and order rescheduling for quarantined cold-chain lines
elements.justification: Reuse of the pattern actor 'Sales Administrator' for the order-side consequences of a cold-chain hold.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer - informed of the cold-chain hold and of the confirmed delivery date once a decision is taken
elements.justification: Adapted from the pattern actor 'Customer'; the receiving party must be informed without receiving any release statement before the quality decision.

elements.text: IT Security Officer - owns integrity and access control of temperature log data and of the monitoring interfaces
elements.justification: Not present in the retrieved patterns; required by the query actor list and by the parent goal's 'secure' dimension, since a continuous log is only credible if it cannot be altered.

elements.text: AI Product Owner - accountable for the ordering assistant's cold-chain response rules and for keeping it out of release decisions
elements.justification: Not present in the retrieved patterns; needed because this organization operates an LLM-based ordering assistant that could otherwise state a release or compliance status.

elements.text: Vaccines and insulin must be kept between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius
elements.justification: Stated in the query; it fixes the excursion threshold used by the alerting and quarantine tasks.

elements.text: Loggers record at least every five minutes, so a gap of more than one interval counts as a break in the continuous log
elements.justification: Reuse of the pattern belief 'Loggers record every five minutes', which gives an operational definition of 'continuous' for G04-K1.

elements.text: Regulation requires a batch record for every medicine, including its temperature history and any release decision
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine'; justifies persisting the quality decision as auditable evidence.

elements.text: Only the Quality Assurance Officer may release goods after an excursion; no automatic release is permitted regardless of excursion duration or magnitude
elements.justification: The pattern's conflict resolution allowing automatic release under 15 minutes and 2 degrees is deliberately rejected, because the query constraint reserves release to the Quality Assurance Officer and G04-K3 targets zero releases without a quality decision.

elements.text: Goods with an unresolved excursion cannot be picked, dispatched or invoiced
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the pattern constraint, extended to the downstream order-to-cash steps of this distributor.

elements.text: Temperature log records are append-only; corrections require a documented change request and leave the original reading visible
elements.justification: Adapted from 'A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request'; protects the evidential value of the continuous log measured by G04-K1.

elements.text: The LLM-based ordering assistant may report cold-chain hold status only as recorded in the system and must never state, imply or promise a release or compliance outcome
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern covers an AI assistant; this constraint is needed so the conversational channel cannot substitute for the Quality Assurance Officer's decision.

output.rational_statement: G04 contributes to the parent goal G01 'Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure' by making the cold chain an evidenced and controlled segment of the order-to-delivery flow: continuous logging from dispatch to hospital acceptance, backed by batch-linked records and logger coverage checks, satisfies G04-K1 and supplies the regulatory evidence the parent goal needs; alerting the Responsible Pharmacist and Quality Assurance Officer with timed acknowledgement and automatic escalation satisfies G04-K2 so that a deviation is handled while the product can still be saved; and automatic quarantine, a signed Quality Assurance Officer release decision and a dispatch block that also binds the order portal and the LLM ordering assistant keep G04-K3 at zero. Following SKB-02/G2, the quality decision - not the sensor - is the control that turns a detected excursion into a safe outcome, but unlike that pattern no automatic release tolerance is adopted here, because the query constraint reserves release to the Quality Assurance Officer for products that, per the stated belief, must remain between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius.
